description: A woodshop can purchase two types of saws, a miter saw and a circular saw. A miter saw can cut 50 planks of wood and produces 60 units of sawdust per day. A circular saw can cut 70 planks of wood and produces 100 units of sawdust per day. The woodshop must cut at least 1500 planks of wood per day. However, to avoid too much pollution in the woodshop they can produce at most 2000 units of sawdust per day. How many of each type of saw should be purchased to minimize the total number of saws needed?

NumSawTypes.definition: Number of types of saws available

PlanksCutPerSaw.definition: Number of planks cut per day by each saw type

SawdustPerSaw.definition: Units of sawdust produced per day by each saw type

MinPlanks.definition: Minimum number of planks to be cut per day

MaxSawdust.definition: Maximum units of sawdust to be produced per day

objective.description: "Minimize the total number of saws purchased (miter saws and circular saws combined)"

constraints.description: The total number of planks cut per day by all saws must be at least MinPlanks
The total amount of sawdust produced per day by all saws must be at most MaxSawdust
The number of saws purchased of each type must be nonnegative integers

NumSaws.definition: Number of saws of each type to be purchased
